correctness.rationale: The explicit 14-vertex Fano-incidence construction has 14 distinct nine-vertex facets and 4480 nonempty faces. The standalone program verifies all 22974 signed-cover orientation relations form a DAG under the 2224-pair matching, with critical counts one in dimension zero, 29 in dimension four and two in dimension five. Exact signed integer substitutions give zero 29x2 Morse boundary. The four-skeleton is a wedge of 29 S4, and pi_4-to-H_4 is an isomorphism, so both five-cell attaching maps are null and the integral wedge result follows. A separate mod-two simplicial rank computation confirms Betti 29 and 2 but is not used to deduce the integer boundary.

originality.rationale: The exactly defined face relation is the open neighborhood complex of the square of the Heawood graph, or equivalently Previte’s D-neighborhood complex at exact distances one and two. The closest inspected 2014 dissertation establishes the general construction and reports cases for the Petersen and Platonic graphs and tree/cycle decompositions, but does not identify this Fano incidence instance or its integral homotopy wedge. Shukla’s maximum-degree-three result applies to the neighborhood complex of the cubic graph itself, not of its nine-regular square. No equivalent or dominating statement was found in the actual searches; unindexed literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: Publication priority is not conclusively established; a differently named general theorem about the square of an incidence graph may exist.
Only sampled relevant portions, not all pages, of the later degree-three paper were read; its exact definition and quoted theorem are sufficient for the degree-based inapplicability.
No separate independent expert audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The object is not a free parameter slice: it is exactly the open neighborhood complex of the square of the canonical 14-vertex Fano-plane incidence graph, or equivalently the radius-two punctured common-center construction. Its mixed integral homotopy has 29 spheres in degree four and two in degree five despite 14 pure eight-dimensional facets, providing a structural classification and non-shellability example that ordinary Lovasz-neighborhood results for cubic graphs do not imply. The integral attaching-map nullity is stronger than an isolated Betti calculation; potential usefulness is in studying distance expansions of incidence structures, while no theorem for all projective orders is claimed.
